To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the relativistic mean-field theory of nuclear dynamics, when applied to intermediate energy heavy-ion collisions, is a very useful and powerful tool for the description of the dynamics of these collisions.

(1) A three-fluid model of relativistic heavy-ion collisions, which is a generalization of the relativistic mean-field two-fluid model (R2FM) of Refs. [2,3] and is based on relativistic mean-field (RMF) theory of nuclear matter, is formulated.

(1) the three-fluid model provides a better description of the dynamics of heavy-ion collisions at intermediate energies than the two-fluid model and (2) it provides a good description of the dynamics at intermediate energies.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a relativistic kinetic theory for heavy ion collisions at intermediate energy.
the application of relativistic mean-field (RMF) kinetic theory to heavy-ion collisions.
the study of the dynamics of heavy ion collisions at intermediate energies, with the goal of developing a model that is capable of describing both the early and late stages of the collision process.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the RMF model is an adequate description of heavy-ion reactions, at the energies considered in this paper, and that the RMF three-fluid model provides a better approximation to the complete kinetic theory than the RMF two-fluid model.
the present model, although not perfect, gives the best possible description of the data in terms of a relativistic mean-field theory.

the RMF3FM model is a useful tool for the study of the dynamics of heavy-ion collisions in the intermediate-energy regime, and it can be used to investigate the role of the mean fields in the equilibration process.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the relativistic mean-field two-fluid model (or the relativistic mean- field three-fluid model) is a good approximation to the full relativistic mean-field Landau-Vlasvo kinetics for the case of the thermalization of the counter-streaming nuclear fluid.
the relativistic mean-field models are a good approximation to the kinetic theory, but the two-fluid models are not good enough to describe the equilibration process.
we have developed a relativistic mean-field theory of heavy-ion collisions which is a natural extension to the relativistic kinetic theory and is free from fitting parameters.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a three-fluid description of heavy-ion dynamics at intermediate energies is necessary to account for the dynamics of the mean field.
a three-fluid model with mean-field interactions is capable of describing the thermalization process of the colliding nuclei in heavy-ion collisions.
the three-fluid model is more accurate than the two-fluid model, which is more accurate than a single-fluid model.
